tagline: Three slow miles through a town named for a kindness.
intro: This one is a town drive, about three miles around the old streets of Socorro, past the San Miguel church and the plaza. Buildings from the Spanish colonial years still stand along the way.

The name means help. In 1598 Oñate's settlers came out of the Jornada del Muerto and the Piro people of Teypana gave them food and water, so the Spaniards renamed the pueblo. Later came the railroad, in 1880, and for a while some of the richest lead and zinc mining in the country.

moments.title: San Miguel de Socorro
moments.text: The oldest building in town stands on the ruins of a 1620s mission, and a piece of that older adobe wall shows behind glass to the left of the altar.

moments.title: Socorro Wheel of History
moments.text: A block north of the plaza a bronze wheel tells the whole account, from the Piro pueblos and the colonial village to the mining boomtown and the science town of today.

moments.title: Garcia Opera House
moments.text: Its owner hoped to draw opera to the 1886 hall and got travelling theatre and masked balls instead, with no record of an opera company ever stopping.
